body: Started 1985 with ₹5,000 + borrowed brother's clients' money. Tata Tea 1986 5,000 sh ₹43→143. Biggest wealth from 1991–92 bear trade. 'I love trading more than investing'. Titan bought 2002 at ~₹30–50 unadjusted (₹3 adjusted); 5.1% stake ₹11,087 cr ≈ 1/3 of ~₹30k cr portfolio at death. A2Z −94%. Aptech SEBI settlement 14 Jul 2021: him ~₹18.5 cr; ~₹37 cr all parties. Akasa Air co-founder.
title: Rakesh Jhunjhunwala

body: Flag: MOSTLY-CLEAN (governance) with an aggressive deal/capital-allocation record. Ajay Piramal is a serial asset trader: sold the domestic formulations business to Abbott (2010, ~$3.7bn), traded a Vodafone India stake (2011-14), took and exited a Shriram group stake, then pivoted Piramal Enterprises (PEL) into real-estate wholesale lending (2014-2019) -- a concentrated book that hurt after IL&FS (2018-19). PEL acquired DHFL via IBC (2021, ~Rs 34,250 cr plan), giving a large retail book plus legacy recoveries. Structure changes: pharma vertically demerged into Piramal Pharma (2022; 4 PPL shares per PEL share); PEL merged into wholly owned Piramal Finance effective 16-Sep-2025 (1:1 swap; PEL delisted, Piramal Finance listed), with Anand Piramal as chair. No promoter pledging; no SEBI/ED findings against promoters found. Points to watch: frequent restructurings (each one resets comparables), legacy wholesale write-downs, alternate-investment-fund (AIF) structures flagged by RBI in 2023 (evergreening rules), and promoter-group real-estate (Piramal Realty, unlisted) interactions with the lender. Good conduct: demergers gave mirror shareholding; buybacks/dividends from PEL historically; rights issues offered to all. Status Nov-2026: Piramal Finance is the listed lending entity; no open governance actions found.

data.red_flags: concentrated wholesale RE lending; frequent restructurings; AIF exposure (RBI 2023)
